result.summary: I'm treating this as an electrical safety emergency. The kitchen socket has been warm with a burning smell for more than 8 hours. The tenant is at home with her 10-year-old son. The circuit hasn't been switched off, nobody has inspected it, and the landlord hasn't replied. I escalated to the ops queue at high priority. The CRM then let me assign a qualified electrician, Rian Sol of Bracken Spark Services, without landlord approval. His job is limited to making the socket safe, switching off its circuit and testing it. I sent the tenant safety and isolation advice, which she says she hadn't had until now. I sent the electrician an urgent brief and told the landlord why we acted without his approval. A hold checks in about 6 hours whether the electrician has confirmed.
result.situation: Nora Bell first reported the warm socket and hot smell at 08:14. At 16:42 she says she is home with her son and the smell is still there. Nobody has switched off a breaker, and she says she has had no emergency advice. The landlord only authorised his general handyman, Rowan Pike. Rowan doesn't do wiring work, has no test equipment and couldn't get in. The landlord hasn't answered the 13:14 voicemail or the 15:02 email asking for authority. The ticket was still at intake.

judgement.why_this_decision: A warm socket face with a burning smell that has lasted all day (events 001, 004, 008, 017, 025) is electrical danger. The circuit isn't isolated, a child is at home, and the tenant has had no safety advice (events 009, 025). The only person sent was a handyman who doesn't do wiring work and never got in (events 011, 015, 023). The landlord hasn't answered the electrician authority request (events 020, 024). The emergency rules say: give containment advice, escalate at high priority, get urgent attendance and tell the landlord. Approval doesn't block emergency safety work, so the electrician's scope is limited to making safe and testing, and any repair needs the landlord's approval.
